title: The Fox Who Had Lost His Tail

keywords: the fox who had lost his tail
full_text:
A fox whose tail had been cut off in a steel trap was so ashamed of his deformity that he called an assembly of foxes, eloquently urging them all to cut off their tails as useless, heavy burdens.

An old fox stood up and remarked: "You would never give us this advice, neighbor, if you had not lost your own tail!"
moral: Distrust counsel that advises you to mutilate yourself to match another’s misfortune.
